summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, migraines, sleep apnea, and recent chest pain evaluation was admitted for acute lower back pain that began a week prior without trauma. The pain was localized to the lower back and buttocks, with no radiation, weakness, or bowel/bladder changes. She had been seen in the ED previously and underwent an MRI that revealed a herniated disc at L5-S1 with possible impingement on the right S1 nerve root. She was admitted for pain management and further care. During her stay, she received oral hydromorphone and acetaminophen for pain, started on a six-day steroid taper, and prescribed tizanidine for muscle relaxation. A back brace was recommended, and home physical therapy was arranged. Her diabetes and hypertension were managed with continued outpatient medications, and she was treated for opioid-induced constipation with Miralax and Colace. She improved clinically and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up planned with spine specialists and clear instructions on warning signs requiring urgent care.
